solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Nick's term therefore, is an unpleasant experience of the past?

definitions.text: Nick's term therefore, is an unpleasant experience of the past?

blocks.clueFragment: Nick's term therefore, is an unpleasant experience of the past
blocks.note: surface reading: a sentence in prison, looked back on as a bad memory
setter's reading: when a prison stretch is finished, the warders' phrase announcing release is the answer, and the ordeal is over

explanation.surface: A former prisoner reflects that his spell inside is now an unpleasant memory.
explanation.walkthrough: The nick is British slang for prison and a term is the sentence served there; once it is served, the phrase TIME IS UP applies and it all lies in the past.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom announces that an allotted period has run out, which is what happens at the end of a prison sentence.

clue.text: see 12ac.
Sex available here around top shelf

indicators.note: something turned around is moved out of its starting order, so the letters get rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written; the top shelf is where newsagents keep porn magazines

explanation.surface: A newsagent's top shelf is where the sex magazines are found.
explanation.walkthrough: In British shops, adult magazines sit on the top shelf, out of children's reach, which makes the surface feel like a description of a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleshpot is a place offering sexual entertainment or vice, so sex is available there.

clue.text: Thumbs up Schwarzenegger's arse? Amusement curtailed

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short, so most of the long word is chopped away, leaving its opening

blocks.note: an American, as Schwarzenegger now is, says ass for arse
a synonym for amusement

explanation.surface: Someone approves of Arnold Schwarzenegger's backside, though the fun is cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first three letters of ENTERTAINMENT survive the curtailment, a heavier trim than the usual one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A thumbs up is a gesture of approval or agreement, which is what assent means.

clue.text: Pussy after pussy

blocks.note: surface reading: one cat following another
setter's reading: a male cat (one pussy) chasing females, and slang for a man always pursuing sex

explanation.walkthrough: The second pussy carries its vulgar sense, so the answer is both a male cat and a womaniser.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomcat is a male cat, and the word is also slang for a promiscuous man who chases women.

clue.text: Trouser-opening youth: "nothing's popped out – thing's crap and unreliable"

indicators.note: something that has popped out has left its place, so that letter goes missing from the word
crap here means badly made or shoddy, so the word's letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the fly is the opening at the front of trousers
a youth is a boy
nothing is zero, the letter O
taken as written

explanation.surface: A boy with his flies undone is told something has slipped out of his trousers and the zip is useless.
explanation.walkthrough: The O drops out of BOY, and THING is rearranged; FLY + BY + NIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A fly-by-night operator is untrustworthy and liable to vanish, hence unreliable.

clue.text: Direct pisspoor item shown at film's end?

indicators.note: pisspoor means badly done, so the word is treated sloppily and its letters jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A critic sneers at a badly directed film, with something flashed up as it finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Direct' looks like part of the film-making picture, but it is the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A credit is one of the listed acknowledgements of cast and crew that roll at the close of a movie.

clue.text: Before you know it, the clubbing celeb's so taken by a paparazzo?

definitions.text: the clubbing celeb's so taken by a paparazzo?

blocks.note: first meaning: very quickly

blocks.clueFragment: the clubbing celeb's so taken by a paparazzo
blocks.note: second meaning: a photographer snaps the star using a camera's burst of light

explanation.surface: A celebrity leaving a nightclub is snapped by a photographer before they notice.
explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning reads the phrase literally: the picture is taken with a flashgun.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means instantly, in the time a burst of light lasts.

clue.text: Obama's 'tender' party will, shortly, with God's backing

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the god's name is read from right to left

blocks.note: a do is a party
will is shortened to the contraction 'll
Ra is the Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: A US president's tender-hearted party has divine support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' in quotes is legal tender, money, not gentleness.
explanation.definitionFit: The dollar is American legal tender, the currency of the country Obama led.

clue.text: Horny beast gets stuff for pre-marital affair?

blocks.note: a stag is an animal with antlers, literally horny
to do someone is slang for having sex, as is to stuff

explanation.surface: A randy animal gets laid ahead of a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: A stag do is the British name for a groom's party before his wedding, a bachelor party.
explanation.definitionFit: The question mark admits a stag do is an event held before marriage rather than a romantic fling.

clue.text: Putting it mildly, Nigel Farage needs dodgy money to take naughty pics, etc.

indicators.note: naughty means misbehaving, so the letters refuse to stay in their order

blocks.note: the currency a Brexiteer would consider dodgy
taken as written

explanation.surface: Farage is short of cash and resorts to taking smutty photographs.
explanation.walkthrough: Nigel Farage is the British politician who led the campaign to leave the European Union.
explanation.definitionFit: Farage is a fierce opponent of the European Union, so calling him doubtful about it is an understatement.

clue.text: (&2dn/25ac.) When everything goes wrong, crap and shock Doris?

blocks.note: crap means poor in quality
a shock is a thick mass of hair
Doris Day, the American singer and actress

explanation.surface: On a disastrous day, something awful happens that scandalises a woman called Doris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock' looks like a fright but is a head of hair; Doris is the film star's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a day on which nothing goes right, as if one's hair would not behave.

clue.text: Soak was screwed up, overthrown leader

indicators.note: something screwed up is messed up, so the letters are put in a new order
an overthrown thing is upended, so in this across clue the letters run backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
PM is the Prime Minister, the country's leader

explanation.surface: A drunkard made a mess of things and the leader was toppled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soak' tempts as a noun for a drunk, which fits the surface, but it is the verb: to drench.
explanation.definitionFit: To swamp something is to flood or drench it with water, the same as to soak it.

clue.text: Palace spy's boxing ring's awful climax

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing in a box, so the palace phrase wraps around the ring
awful means dreadful, a mess, so the combined letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: A spy at the palace is caught up in a boxing ring and meets a terrible end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxing ring' reads as one phrase about a fight; split, boxing is the container signal and ring the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apocalypse is the final catastrophic culmination of the world, its ultimate end-point.

clue.text: Pissed knight, tosser, is well-connected

indicators.note: pissed means drunk, and a drunk staggers, so the letters reel into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
both are British insults for a fool

explanation.surface: A drunken knight, an idiot, nonetheless has good social connections.
explanation.walkthrough: Tosser and tit are both British slang for a contemptible idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: A tight-knit group is closely bound together, its members strongly linked to one another.

clue.text: Guy Fawkes' place before extravagant monarch?

blocks.note: Pl. is the street-name abbreviation for Place
OTT is over the top
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Guy Fawkes's spot, ahead of a lavish king or queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Guy Fawkes was one of the men behind the 1605 plan to blow up Parliament and King James I, remembered on Bonfire Night.
explanation.definitionFit: Fawkes conspired in the Gunpowder Plot, so he is the type of a conspirator; the definition is read as a description, not a possessive.

clue.text: Brand gives piss up thumbs up

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word is written from bottom to top

blocks.note: piss is British slang for weak beer
a thumbs-up sign means OK

explanation.surface: A brand sponsors a booze-up and gives it the nod.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piss up' looks like a drinking session; split, piss is the drink and up the turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Reebok is a well-known sportswear company name, so it is an example of a brand.

clue.text: Grateful LibDems, dumping script, go berserk

indicators.note: dumping means throwing away, so those letters are dropped from the party name
going berserk means running wild, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written; the Liberal Democrats are a UK party
MS is manuscript, a hand-written script
taken as written

explanation.surface: Thankful Liberal Democrats abandon their prepared speech and run amok.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grateful' wants to describe the LibDems, but it stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being obliged to someone means feeling indebted and thankful for a favour.

clue.text: In no time at all, Huhne was privy to cut steel production

definitions.text: In no time at all, Huhne was

indicators.note: steel production is the making of it, so the word is remade into a new order
something that cuts into a word splits it and sits inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
a privy is a toilet, in British English a loo

explanation.surface: Chris Huhne, the jailed minister, was in on a plan to cut steel output.
explanation.walkthrough: Chris Huhne was a Liberal Democrat cabinet minister jailed in 2013 for perverting justice and freed after about nine weeks. 'Privy' tempts as 'in on a secret'; it is a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Huhne was released from prison after serving only a short part of his sentence, so he was freed quickly.

clue.text: The start of the controversial anti-Thatcher ditty row

definitions.text: The start of the controversial anti-Thatcher ditty

blocks.clueFragment: The start of the controversial anti-Thatcher ditty
blocks.note: first meaning: the opening words of '...! The Witch Is Dead', bought into the charts by her opponents when she died
second meaning: a noisy argument or fierce fight

explanation.walkthrough: After Margaret Thatcher died in 2013, the Wizard of Oz song climbed the UK charts, causing a fuss over whether the BBC should play it.
explanation.definitionFit: A ding-dong is British slang for a heated quarrel, and the words also open the Wizard of Oz song.

clue.text: Warning: there's one large member on Thatcher advisor

blocks.note: a means one
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
an arm is a limb, a member of the body
Tim Bell, the PR man who ran Thatcher's election campaigns

explanation.surface: A caution: someone has a sizeable appendage on display on a Thatcher aide.
explanation.walkthrough: Member tempts with its rude sense; here it is a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarm bell is a signal of danger, and figuratively any early sign that something is wrong.

clue.text: A feat to conceal double-D with one fan

indicators.note: to conceal something is to hide it inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: a feat is an act, a deed
two Ds
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A woman with a double-D bra size manages to hide it from an admirer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' looks like a separate letter, but 'A feat' together means ACT, which then holds the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An addict is a devotee or enthusiast, as in a jazz addict, just as a fan is.

clue.text: Bloody hell! A promise from Cyclops!

blocks.note: first meaning: an exclamation of surprise
second meaning: the setter, speaking for himself, gives his solemn pledge

explanation.walkthrough: Cyclops is the setter, so the promise is his own pledge, given in his first person.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a mild expression of astonishment, and also a person's pledge of honour.

clue.text: Foot's a venerated famous person

blocks.note: first meaning: read as two words, the bottom extremity of a lower limb
second meaning: a revered celebrity

explanation.walkthrough: The first meaning splits the answer into LEG END, which is where the foot is; Foot with its capital also hints at the politician Michael Foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is someone so celebrated that they are spoken of with awe.

clue.text: God knocker has one

blocks.note: both are slang for a breast
an means one

explanation.surface: A deity with an impressive bosom.
explanation.walkthrough: Knocker sounds like the thing on a front door but is British slang for a breast.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titans were the giant deities of Greek mythology who preceded the Olympians.

clue.text: see 12ac.
Michael, not Paul as intended? Hack's caught off guard

blocks.note: Michael Foot is the incorrect Foot when Paul Foot was meant
ED is an editor, a newspaper hack

explanation.surface: A journalist got Michael Foot and Paul Foot mixed up and was left floundering.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Foot led the Labour Party; his nephew Paul Foot was a campaigning journalist at Private Eye, so picking one for the other is getting the wrong Foot.
explanation.definitionFit: To be wrong-footed is to be thrown off balance by something unexpected, surprised and unprepared.

clue.text: Member Rob's erection

indicators.note: an erection is something raised upright, so in this down clue the word reads upwards

blocks.note: to loot is to rob

explanation.surface: A man called Rob is aroused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rob' looks like a man's name but is the verb to steal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tool is slang for the penis, which is also called the male member.

clue.text: Enduring political leader's pure voice – no top grade leader of Tories

indicators.note: no means without, so the named letters are taken out

blocks.note: a castrato is a male singer with a pure high voice
A is the highest grade
the first letter of Tories

explanation.surface: A long-serving leader speaks with an unsullied voice, minus the best mark, leading the Conservatives.
explanation.walkthrough: The A and the second T are removed from CASTRATO.
explanation.definitionFit: Fidel Castro ruled Cuba for almost fifty years, an unusually long-lasting head of state.

clue.text: Not conscious of being elected, was rat-arsed with nothing on

indicators.note: rat-arsed is British slang for very drunk, so the letters stagger out of order

blocks.note: a party elected to power is in
taken as written
nothing is zero, the letter O
taken as written

explanation.surface: A newly elected politician passed out drunk and naked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With nothing on' reads as naked, but it supplies two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a swoon is to have fainted, so the person is unconscious.
